rewrites.summary:
For a trans traveler Rivers carries no state-level protective statute: the national framework applies in full — a 2014 statute punishes same-sex unions with up to 14 years' imprisonment, bans same-sex cohabitation and any public show of a same-sex amorous relationship, and reaches registering, operating or supporting gay organisations — and a foreign government's August 2026 travel advisory warns LGBT+ travellers to this country of arrest, violence, blackmail and intimidation.

Practical safety in this state is documented directly: a 21-year-old gay man who travelled to this state in January 2015 to meet someone he had contacted on a social media platform was attacked and sexually abused there and did not report it to police; the national pattern after the 2014 statute includes arbitrary arrest and extortion by police, including 8 of 21 young men arrested but never charged at a birthday gathering in another state. A 2022 court ruling that certain sections of the 2014 statute are unconstitutional and unenforceable nationwide did not remove the documented enforcement climate in practice, and the sources record no legal protections for LGBT+ people under the framework.
